memory_update.text: AAOI should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a direct underfollowed optical transceiver candidate with explicit 1.6T hyperscaler order evidence, but survival depends on shipment conversion, customer concentration risk, and margin follow-through.

TSEM is a high-priority underfollowed silicon-photonics capacity candidate because signed SiPho contracts and customer prepayments may indicate foundry-capacity scarcity tied to 1.6T/NPO/CPO optical networking.
VIAV belongs in the discovery lane as a second-order optical test and qualification vendor; the key evidence gap is materiality of 1.6T AI optical testing within total company revenue.

For AI optical networking, the likely chokepoint map should include pluggable transceivers, InP/EML lasers, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, external laser sources, photonic packaging, and 800G/1.6T validation equipment.

Need a later Layer 1C/2 pass to separate optical-component suppliers with true AI datacenter revenue from legacy telecom/CATV optics, because the same product labels can hide very different demand and margin profiles.

node: AI optical networking components and photonics supply chain
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around AI optical networking components, emphasizing direct transceiver suppliers, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, and optical-network test vendors. The discovery lane is strongest in AAOI, TSEM, and VIAV because each sits one step away from the obvious AI switch/ASIC vendors and has explicit 800G/1.6T AI data-center language. COHR is included as a reference anchor because it is a better-known vertically integrated photonics supplier and helps benchmark what the market may already recognize.
